matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Transfer a single vertical matchstick that forms an I from one numeral to another to adjust their numeric values.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a value that can be corrected by adding or removing a vertical stick from an I numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to a V, leaving the I missing a stick (invalid) or the V with an extra vertical stick (invalid).

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try moving a stick within the same character to change its shape (e.g., turning X into V or I, or turning V into X).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick relocation inside a numeral can change its value without affecting other characters.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of turning a V into an X by repositioning one diagonal, and instead trying inter‑character moves.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, ensure that both the character that lost the stick and the character that gained the stick remain valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before checking arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X to V and leaving X as a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: Diagonal sticks must appear in pairs to form a V or X; a lone diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any move that removes or adds a diagonal, verify that no character ends up with a single diagonal.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X and leaving it as a single diagonal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and a vertical stick can be repurposed to adjust a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from a plus sign and leaving a stray vertical that cannot be attached to any numeral, resulting in an invalid equation.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new Roman numeral (e.g., a single V stick can become an I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When after moving a stick you have a free stick that can serve as a valid numeral on its own.
matchstick.example: Leaving a detached diagonal stick unattached, which does not form any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character options without success.
matchstick.example: Attempting to move a horizontal from '=' to '-' without first checking intra‑character changes, leading to an incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick move
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick from the equals sign to a minus (or plus) sign swaps the two operators while preserving validity.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '=' and '-' (or '+') and swapping them could balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Swapping '=' and '-' but forgetting to recompute the arithmetic, resulting in a false equation.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting a plus sign to a minus by removing its vertical stick, attach that stick to a nearby numeral to increase its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a vertical stick becomes free after a plus‑to‑minus conversion and can be used to modify a numeral.
matchstick.example: Attaching the freed vertical stick to a V, which cannot accept a vertical, creating an invalid character.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute their numeric values to ensure the equation holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any candidate transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Assuming the new equation is correct without verifying that the numeric values match.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to consider moving sticks between characters first, missing simpler shape changes within a single character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always try intra‑character stick relocation before exploring inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as immutable in orientation, missing valid rotations that keep the stick angled.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that angled sticks can be repositioned with any diagonal orientation, but cannot become vertical/horizontal.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual validity of symbols and forgets to check the numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after any move.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes that swapping operators will balance the equation without checking the resulting values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After swapping operators, recompute the arithmetic to verify correctness.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the I↔L transformation (adding/removing a horizontal stick to/from an I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks that an I can become an L by adding a horizontal, which can be useful.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Consider adding or removing a horizontal stick to/from an I to form L when needed.
